bounds: Early-stage companies are uncertain by nature.
A startup can run out of cash, fail to find customers, lose a key supplier, face litigation, or be unable to raise its next round.
If it closes, creditors and other security holders may have priority over you, and there may be nothing left for common shareholders or a SAFE holder.
That means losing the full amount is possible, not just seeing the number temporarily fall.
A startup can also keep operating while your particular security never converts, pays no distribution, or finds no buyer.
Review risks that are specific to the company, not only a generic warning.
Ask what must go right for the plan to work, how much cash is available, and what happens if the raise is smaller than expected.
Only consider money you can afford to lose without putting essential needs at risk.
Diversifying can reduce dependence on one company, but it cannot eliminate startup risk or guarantee a return.
